body: Ghost in the Shell is Exact's PlayStation action game, first released in Japan on 17 July 1997. The player joins Public Security Section 9 as a recruit piloting a Fuchikoma, a small robotic combat vehicle. Missions follow an investigation into the Human Liberation Front, placing the action within the world of Masamune Shirow's manga. The vehicle changes how that world is explored: walls and ceilings become surfaces to travel across. Rather than following a human figure through corridors, the player learns to read a room as a machine capable of climbing it.

The Fuchikoma can move from the ground onto vertical surfaces and overhead structures, allowing the player to approach enemies from unusual positions. A route that appears closed at floor level may remain open above it. Combat therefore asks for awareness of the whole space, not only the ground ahead. Learning how the view changes during a climb is part of gaining control. The movement gives the game its particular character, turning architecture into a choice of firing positions and making the player's route an active part of an encounter.

Shirow supplied character and mechanical designs, while Production I.G. worked with Exact on the production. Animated sequences connect the missions to the cast around Section 9, and the English release uses the voice cast familiar from the 1995 film's English dub. The game itself draws its setting and tone from the manga rather than continuing that film. Its electronic soundtrack received an album release alongside other supporting material. Reviewers praised the animation, music and climbing mechanics, helping establish it as a distinctive adaptation within the PlayStation's early three-dimensional library.
